newsitem.title: USA: NO PLANS YET TO HIRE REPLACEMENTS, UPS SAYS.
newsitem.headline: NO PLANS YET TO HIRE REPLACEMENTS, UPS SAYS.

text.p: United Parcel Service of America Inc Vice Chairman John Alden said Monday there were no current plans for the company to hire replacements for striking members of the Teamsters union.
"Right now we have no plans to hire (replacement) people," Alden said when asked by ABC's "Good Morning America" about reports that UPS might hire substitute workers.
"We would like our people to come back to work (but) I can't promise what the future will bring," he added.
Since the strike by 185,000 Teamsters started last Monday, the company has relied largely on management to operate at greatly reduced levels.
Labor Secretary Alexis Herman warned on Sunday against any move by the company to hire replacement workers.

Executives of Atlanta-based UPS, which before the strike delivered about 80 percent of all packages shipped by ground nationwide, said they wanted to avoid hiring replacement workers but declined to rule out such a move.
"The last thing we want to do, the last thing I want to do, is replace UPS workers," Chief Executive Officer James Kelly, said on Sunday on the CBS program "Face the Nation."
But he left open the possibility, saying that UPS was losing "hundreds of millions of dollars a week."
